controls_available: Mouse-wheel scrolling on each visible XY, XZ, or YZ linked slice canvas changes the corresponding x, y, or z focus.
Dragging empty mesh glass with the mouse orbits the three-dimensional reconstruction.
Dragging from one visible mesh node to another with the mouse adds a merge edge.
Clicking RED SEED or GREEN SEED selects the active split-seed colour, and clicking a visible slice node places that seed.
Clicking CUT BETWEEN SEEDS removes the edge between the two placed seeds.
Clicking CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH submits the repair.

autonomous_processes.period: Every interval with no new agent input during active repair
autonomous_processes.state_change: None: nodes, edges, linked-slice focus, seeds, camera, and topology remain unchanged.
autonomous_processes.visible_evidence: The mechanic only mutates model state from wheel, pointer, and click handlers; the branch-specific CSS has no animation.

actions: drag from one visible mesh node to another

clause_i.reason: For a grouped merge-drag mode, no action-only q(I_t) can choose the optimal endpoints across all seeded occurrences: the generator varies the target fibre and missing endpoints, and its public node identifiers are opaque. The grader accepts only the seed-specific missing edges. The same observation dependence applies to the false-edge split mode.

clause_ii.reason: A single current screenshot is a bounded window here because observation_window_ms is 0. It shows the mesh, labels, three linked slice canvases, current edges, and current focus, so a reactive screenshot-only policy can choose the next navigation, seed, or merge action. Multiple chronological frames are not needed to predict a delayed state because the task state does not advance autonomously.

clause_iii.reason: There is no H_t to H_t^tau with 0 < tau < Delta in which non-clock task state evolves without an agent action. Merges, cuts, slice changes, camera changes, and seed placement are synchronous event-handler effects; waiting does not remove or reduce the value of any repair action. The post-edit inspection lock is itself set by the preceding edit and is cleared by a later slice action, not by elapsed time.

common_visible_process: None. The visible autonomous process required to connect clauses (i), (ii), and (iii) is absent; the only relevant state changes are agent-triggered edits/navigation and an action-triggered certification response.

pre_run.reason: No instance has an autonomous outcome phase. At difficulty 4 the generator always creates two missing joins and two false joins, and successful grading requires four outcome-affecting topology edits, with linked-view inspections between them; certification is only administrative.

source_evidence.claim: The exact profile is difficulty 4 with four fibres, nine segments per fibre, two missing joins, two false joins, eleven slices, and full interaction; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The runner repeats the 0 ms, one-frame observation configuration and uses synchronous task execution.

Generation is deterministic from the seed, constructs static node coordinates and initial edges, varies the target and opaque node identifiers, and stores true/missing/false topology only in the grading truth.

The browser creates the static model and changes focus, edges, seeds, or camera only in explicit input handlers; merges and splits set an inspection flag, while certification is the only fetch/action-settlement path.
The branch-specific visual surface consists of canvases and controls, with no branch animation or time-driven visual rule.

Grading replays the submitted event sequence, requires source-correct full-mode actions, requires four exact repairs and a post-edit inspection after each, and checks final topology; it has no timing or waiting requirement.
The task verifier loads the exported UI result and invokes the Branch Repair grader, so the outcome is the replayed topology/transcript.

The implementation solver completes the repair through a finite sequence of linked-view observations, one orbit, merge drags, seeded cuts, inspections, and certification; its short waits are browser synchronization waits rather than task mechanics.
The shared clock can drain timers and animation callbacks when running, but the complete Branch Repair mechanic registers no such task timer or animation callback.
